blockingIssues.description: The new Playwright test visits `/api/auth/callback?token_hash=already-used-test-token&redirectedFrom=%2Fguest%2Fdashboard` without a real/invalid auth token fixture, then only asserts that the browser ends up on `/auth` and that the guest link href contains an error query. This can pass on the route's generic missing/invalid-token fallback (`auth_failed`) without proving the required expired/invalid/already-used callback failure handling, so it does not satisfy the feature contract or the follow-up `cover-auth-callback-failure-path` expectation to exercise the real failing callback path.

The updated coverage only verifies the restaurant detail page through a mocked `getRestaurantBySlug` result, while the worker's own browser evidence shows `http://localhost:3000/restaurants/the-fox` resolves to a guest handoff/not-found state instead of the intended detail surface. That means the feature did not actually demonstrate that `/restaurants/[slug]` is aligned with the guest design system in the live runtime, leaving one of the feature's required surfaces unresolved.

The updated page only fixes invalid-slug handling. The feature description explicitly required finishing live validation by establishing at least one stable locally browser-valid public restaurant slug, yet the handoff still reports that the discovered slug (`white-horse-pub-waterbeach`) falls through to the generic try-again/dashboard fallback on the live booking page. Because no code or test coverage was added to make a valid public slug reliably render through detail and booking entry, the implementation does not fully satisfy the assigned expected behavior.

The updated test now treats the broken `/restaurants/seed-perf-r001/book` runtime as success by only asserting the page contains `Guest booking flow` and lacks the old build-overlay text. The feature contract requires a stable live booking-entry page, but the worker's own handoff records that the route still returns HTTP 500 and falls into the generic guest error screen. This change masks the unresolved product failure instead of verifying the required behavior.

rejectedObservations.observation: The worker noted that Playwright leaves `test-results/.last-run.json` dirty after local runs. This is reusable validator knowledge and is already documented in `.factory/library/user-testing.md`, so no additional shared-state update is needed.

The worker followed the skill's allowance to isolate a directly relevant Playwright spec when the broader assigned spec was stale, but the feature brief itself still bundled `guest-reserve-routes.spec.ts` even though user-testing knowledge already documented runtime instability around local restaurant slugs. The shared guidance could more clearly distinguish route-local invalid-slug verification from broader valid-slug live-runtime stabilization work.
